title: How to sink a Battleship fleet in 62 shots, not 97
description:
Five ships fill 17 of the 100 squares, so shooting at random finds the last one late: half of random games need 97 shots. Shoot only one colour of a checkerboard (every ship is at least 2 long, so each covers one), and after a hit fire at the 4 neighbours and follow the line until the ship sinks. In 100,000 simulated games that finishes half of them by shot 62.

Numbers checked in code (exact odds for random shooting, 100,000 simulated games per strategy). Idea and comparison: datagenetics.com/blog/december32011

facts_checked: Fleet 5, 4, 3, 3, 2 = 17 squares on a 10x10 grid; random play ~96 shots for half the games; parity hunt/target median 64; every ship covers a square of each colour since the smallest is 2 long (https://www.datagenetics.com/blog/december32011/index.html)
Random shooting: exact median 97 shots (the last of 17 ship squares in a random order of 100) (verify.py)
Checkerboard: 50 dark squares, every 2-long placement covers one (verify.py)
100,000 simulated games: checkerboard hunt + neighbour targeting median 62 shots; random median 97 (verify.py)
CTA: smallest ship 3 long -> squares with (row + col) divisible by 3, 34 squares, every 3-long placement covers one (verify.py)

beats.say: No luck, and no peeking. You just stop wasting shots.
Ten by ten, five ships, 17 squares. Fire at random, and the last ship hides until the very end.
First, shoot only the dark squares of a checkerboard. Every ship is at least 2 long, so each one covers a dark square. Half the board.
But the real waste is what random players do after a hit.
After a hit, stop hunting. Fire at the 4 squares around it.
A second hit shows the direction. Follow the line until it sinks, then go back to the checkerboard.
In 100,000 games, half are over by shot 62. Random needs 97.
So if the smallest ship left is 3 long, which squares do you still shoot?
